newsitem.title: GERMANY: Graf's father can leave prison - for $3.3 million.
newsitem.headline: Graf's father can leave prison - for $3.3 million.

text.p: A German court trying the father of tennis star Steffi Graf on tax evasion charges ruled on Friday he could be released from custody in return for bail of five million marks ($3.32 million).

Prosecutors objected to the decision and the court went into recess to consider their objection. Peter Graf has spent more than a year in investigative custody in a jail in Mannheim, southwest Germany.
Peter Graf is accused of evading 19 million marks ($12.61 million) of tax on his daughter's earnings between 1989 and 1993. Former family tax adviser Joachim Eckardt is also on trial.
The court said Eckardt could be freed against bail of 300,000 marks ($199,100). Both men would have to report to police twice a week, the court ruled.

Peter Graf was taken into investigative custody in August last year. Prosecutors have repeatedly blocked bids by his lawyers to get him out of jail, saying they fear he could alter evidence or flee the country.
Steffi Graf has said she knew little about her financial affairs, entrusting them to her father from the start of a career which has taken her to the number one spot in women's tennis.
